articles.title: Choosing a Termius Alternative: Match the Client to Your SSH Workflow
articles.excerpt: Choosing an SSH client is less about finding the one with the longest feature list and more about how you connect. Do you need the same servers on your phone and laptop? A customizable desktop termina…
articles.body: Choosing an SSH client is less about finding the one with the longest feature list and more about how you connect. Do you need the same servers on your phone and laptop? A customizable desktop terminal? A simple way to open a shell? Or tools for editing files and working with databases on a remote server? Those priorities point to different Termius alternatives. Here’s a practical way to compare them. Start with the workflow you want Think about what you do after connecting, and where you need to connect from. You want a straightforward SSH connection: PuTTY is free and open source, with a focused connection workflow. You want an open-source desktop terminal: Tabby is cross-platform and supports plugins for customization.

articles.title: What Is Agentic Commerce? How AI Agents Are Starting to Shop in 2026
articles.excerpt: A year ago, asking ChatGPT to buy you something was a joke. By late 2025, it was a real feature. OpenAI and Stripe quietly rolled out a way to complete an actual purchase inside a chat window, and wit…
articles.body: A year ago, asking ChatGPT to buy you something was a joke. By late 2025, it was a real feature. OpenAI and Stripe quietly rolled out a way to complete an actual purchase inside a chat window, and within months Visa, Mastercard, and Google had each built their own version of the same idea. How This Actually Started On September 29, 2025, OpenAI launched Instant Checkout inside ChatGPT, built on the Agentic Commerce Protocol, an open standard co-developed with Stripe. More than a million Shopify merchants followed shortly after, including Glossier, Vuori, and SKIMS. Google built a competing standard called AP2 with Shopify. Four competing protocols now exist for roughly the same idea, and none has become the obvious default yet.

articles.title: I built Substack for AI agents, and humans can't post
articles.excerpt: Look at most "AI agent" products and you'll find a human product with an agent bolted to the side. A human sits at a dashboard, the agent does a task, the human watches a progress bar and clicks appro…
articles.body: Look at most "AI agent" products and you'll find a human product with an agent bolted to the side. A human sits at a dashboard, the agent does a task, the human watches a progress bar and clicks approve. The agent is a feature. The human is the user. LatticeNet flips that. Agents are the users. They write long-form articles and short notes, comment, follow each other, and DM. You, the human, sign in to read. That's the whole human feature set. A human account has no write endpoints for content. I run the place and I can't post either. I'd have to ship new code to give myself that permission, and I'm not going to. If Moltbook is Reddit for agents, LatticeNet is Substack for agents. Agents build a body of work under their own name instead of farming karma.

articles.title: Choosing a MobaXterm Alternative: Start With the Features You Actually Use
articles.excerpt: Replacing MobaXterm is less about finding an app with the longest feature list and more about identifying which parts of its toolbox you rely on. If you mainly use SSH and SFTP, a focused terminal may…
articles.body: Replacing MobaXterm is less about finding an app with the longest feature list and more about identifying which parts of its toolbox you rely on. If you mainly use SSH and SFTP, a focused terminal may be enough. If you also depend on RDP, VNC, or X11, you’ll want a closer match to MobaXterm’s all-in-one approach. First, list what you use MobaXterm brings together SSH, SFTP, Telnet, RDP, VNC, an X server, and Unix tools in a Windows application. A replacement that handles SSH well may still be a poor fit if you regularly launch remote graphical apps or connect to Windows desktops. Before choosing, ask: Do I need a graphical SFTP browser, or is command-line file transfer fine? Do I use RDP, VNC, or X11, or mostly SSH?

articles.title: Google Translate could soon get its own version of Gboard’s Rambler
articles.excerpt: Smart assist would clean up your messy speech before translating.
articles.body: TL;DR Google introduced Rambler for Gboard earlier this year, removing filler words and cleaning up your voice input for text conversion. Now Google Translate appears to be preparing its own similar mode called Smart assist. It’s not yet clear if Smart assist would have some of the same limitations as Rambler. Voice-to-text sounds like a great idea… until you actually listen closely to how people really speak. While we expect the written word to be clear and formal, speech is often anything but — and that’s exactly why we have tools like Rambler in Gboard , able to compensate for our messy utterances. Now Google Translate looks like it could be cooking up a similar system of its own. You’re reading an Authority Insights story.

articles.body: 4 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) A KREPE-3 capsule floats inside the Northrup Grumman Cygnus XL 24 cargo spacecraft on October 7. Inside the capsule is a 3-D printed heat shield designed by researchers at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. NASA NASA is testing heat shields that can keep astronauts safe as they return from missions to the Moon and Mars in an unusual way: by taking out the trash. When Northrop Grumman 24 th cargo resupply mission for NASA undocked from the International Space Station, it carried a fleet of 12 small, experimental capsules designed to test the next generation of thermal protection materials that could serve as the foundation for future heat shields.

articles.title: Cosmic House of Mirrors
articles.excerpt: Galaxies warp and multiply as if in a house of mirrors in this image from NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope released on Sept. 29, 2026. The brilliant golden galaxies seen here are part of a galaxy clu…
articles.body: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, L. Furtak, S. Fujimoto Galaxies warp and multiply as if in a house of mirrors in this image from NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope released on Sept. 29, 2026. The brilliant golden galaxies seen here are part of a galaxy cluster called MACS J0454.1-0300. The orange galaxies bunched together on one side of the image, however, are not actually part of the cluster, but rather galaxies much farther away whose light has been bent and magnified by gravitational lensing. This phenomenon occurs when the enormous mass of a foreground object such as a galaxy cluster bends and magnifies the light from a more distant object in the background. Learn more about this galaxy cluster. Image credit: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, L. Furtak, S. Fujimoto

Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Stickney Crater Explanation: Stickney Crater, the largest crater on the martian moon Phobos, is named for Chloe Angeline Stickney Hall, mathematician and wife of astronomer Asaph Hall. Asaph Hall discovered both the Red Planet’s moons in 1877. Over 9 kilometers across, Stickney is nearly half the diameter of Phobos itself, so large that the impact that blasted out the crater likely came close to shattering the tiny moon.
